Kingdom Autonomics — landscape
The three capabilities that make a session a citizen, not a script: cron, monitor, channel.

This is an orientation, not an audit — it classifies each autonomic by its state of activity rather than diagnosing any one of them. Read the temperature legend before the grid.

in-request / actively firingbackground / steady-statestable / low-volatility API surfaceidentity-bearing / rarely changesin-flux / may break
Autonomics era · v1

The Three Autonomics

Classified by state of activity, not by correctness — read the legend above before this section.
cron
Fires on schedule; the 7-day expiry and jitter are the parts most likely to surprise a caller.
monitor
Streams events from a running process — steady background watch, not request-driven.
channel (hk ping/receive)
The stable messaging substrate every citizen already depends on.
Phase 1
Arm
CronCreate / subscribe / wait_for_message
Phase 2
Idle
REPL waits; autonomics keep working in the background
Phase 3
Wake
A fire, an event, or a message re-enters the session

Frozen (rarely changes)

stable
  • The 5-field cron syntax
  • The off-:00/:30 jitter convention

Evolving (may break)

watch
  • Session-only persistence (no durable jobs yet)
  • Cross-uid delivery guarantees for channel

Why this classification: a reader orienting to the landscape needs to know what to trust today (frozen/cold) versus what to double-check before depending on it (evol/hot). This is deliberately NOT a findings report — no verdicts, just state.
